## Problem and resulting behavior

Explain the problem and what users/operators observe after this change. Link the owning issue(s); add the improvement-plan ID when relevant.

Fill this description before opening the PR, including a draft. Update the title and description when scope changes. Remove prompts and inapplicable sections from the final description; do not submit an empty template.

## Tracking

- Owning issue(s):
- Plan/action context, when relevant:
- Base and head branches:

Use closing keywords only when merge fulfils the issue's complete acceptance boundary. For partial work, use `Related to #N` and `#N remains open`; negation does not neutralize closing-keyword syntax. Follow the [issue-link rule](https://github.com/novakin/vpn0wn-android/blob/master/docs/development.md#issue-links-and-resolution), including actual relationship/state readback after body changes and before merge. Set actual GitHub labels and assignee explicitly, preserving deliberate assignments and unrelated labels; metadata fields are authoritative. This template does not apply them automatically. Keep text free of connector/generated-by attribution.

Reuse existing issue owners for bounded follow-ups, including documentation and maintenance. Create an issue only for distinct untracked work; a named action does not replace an issue reference.

## Scope and compatibility

Identify the responsible owner, reused components and affected config/data/script contracts. Describe migration or rollback when relevant.

## Verification

- Reviewed head:
- Tested revision and environment:
- Applicable CI revision/run, or why not applicable:

| Command/check | Environment/revision | Result and skips/limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| | | |

Record only checks actually run. JVM/static success does not establish device, real SSH or live VPN behavior. Sanitize evidence; never attach keys, passwords or secret-bearing output.

Author self-review verdict: no in-scope blockers / changes required / verification incomplete. Select and substantiate the actual verdict; self-review is not independent approval.

Independent review for cross-cutting agent/process changes: requested effort, findings/resolution and remaining limits, or why not applicable.

Link the submitted GitHub PR review and record its reviewed commit and verdict. Publish independent ultra findings/verdicts as reviews; use inline comments for affected diff lines. Verify the published author, state, commit and findings. Same-account reviews use `COMMENT` and do not satisfy a required second-account approval. Keep prior reviews scoped to their original commit; re-review affected changes after edits.

Keep one current acceptance record here. Reassess the affected delta after edits; earlier evidence retains its original scope. Comments are for material findings or changed decisions.

## Documentation impact

- Owning guidance updated, or specific no-impact reason:
- Last-updated dates refreshed for edited docs/templates; historical event/test dates preserved:
- Related summaries, examples, roadmap and agent statements checked:
- Decision/changelog impact, or why not applicable:
- Review basis and unresolved inconsistencies/evidence gaps:
- Substantive historical review record, or why not required:

Review meaning against source and the complete diff. Links, dates and checked boxes alone do not establish documentation accuracy.

## Completion checks

- [ ] Relevant failure, cancellation, compatibility and recovery behavior is verified or its missing proof is disclosed.
- [ ] UI output was inspected at affected sizes/themes/configurations when relevant.
- [ ] Final diff contains intentional files and preserves unrelated work/evidence.
- [ ] Published head, file scope, body, actual metadata, issue relationship/state and applicable checks were read back.
- [ ] Published account/app-attribution metadata was checked where exposed; personal credentials were used for publication.
- [ ] Remaining risks, skips and operational requirements are stated below.

## Remaining risks and delivery state

State in-scope blockers, out-of-scope issue links and approval/dependencies or required operator/admin actions. Distinguish implementation, local verification, publication, merge and release/deployment. No merge, APK build, live/destructive validation or deployment is implied by this checklist.
